Daniel Muñoz|user=EmiratesFACup|publisher=Emirates FA Cup|date=17 May 2025|access-date=18 May 2025|archive-url=https://archive.today/20250518113930/https://x.com/EmiratesFACup/status/1923814584084779277 |archive-date=18 May 2025}} | referee = [[Stuart Attwell]] ([[Birmingham County Football Association|Birmingham]]){{cite news |title=The match officials for all of our 2025 FA competition finals have been appointed |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2025/apr/29/fa-competitions-cup-finals-match-officials-confirmed-2024-25-20252904 |website=TheFA.com|publisher=[[The Football Association]] |date=29 April 2025 |accessdate=29 April 2025 }} | attendance = 84,163 | weather = Sunny | previous = [[2024 FA Cup final|2024]] | next = [[2026 FA Cup final|2026]] }} The '''2025 FA Cup final''' was a [[Association football|football]] match played at [[Wembley Stadium]] in London, England, on 17 May 2025 between [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] that determined the winners of the [[2024–25 FA Cup]]. It was the [[List of FA Cup finals|144th final]] of English football's primary cup competition, the [[FA Cup|Football Association Challenge Cup]]. Crystal Palace won the match 1–0 after a first-half goal from winger [[Eberechi Eze]] and a penalty save by goalkeeper [[Dean Henderson]], resulting in the club winning their first-ever major trophy, excluding defunct competitions (having previously won the [[1990–91 Full Members' Cup]]). As winners, they earned the right to play against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], the winners of the [[2024–25 Premier League]], in the [[2025 FA Community Shield]]. They would have earned a spot in the league phase of the [[2025–26 UEFA Europa League]] which is given to the FA Cup winners, but lost the right due to a successful appeal by [[Olympique Lyonnais]], who had an equivalent major qualification win but also shared an owner with Palace, which brought [[UEFA]]'s [[Multi-club ownership (association football)|multi-club ownership]] rules into play, allowing an owner only one entry in a tournament; Olympique had a higher domestic league position in the same season, and was thus granted the entry.{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Dale |date=11 July 2025|title=Palace out of Europa League amid Lyon conflict |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/45715071/crystal-palace-demoted-conference-league-amid-ownership-conflict |access-date=15 August 2025|website=ESPN}}{{Cite news |last=Aarons |first=Ed |date=9 July 2025|title=Crystal Palace's Europa League hopes dealt blow after Lyon win relegation appeal |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/jul/09/crystal-palace-europa-league-hopes-dealt-blow-after-lyon-win-relegation-appeal |access-date=15 August 2025|work=The Guardian |issn=0261-3077}} Nevertheless, Palace were instead given a berth to play in the play-off round of the [[2025–26 UEFA Conference League]]. It also meant that Crystal Palace qualified for a major European competition for the first time in club history This decision was appealed by Crystal Palace but was unsuccessful.{{Cite web |date=11 August 2025|title=Crystal Palace lose appeal against demotion from Europa League to Conference League |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c1kzzpp04kgo |access-date=15 August 2025|website=BBC Sport }} For Manchester City, this was their third consecutive FA Cup final, and second defeat in a row, becoming the tenth team to lose consecutive finals. ==Route to the final== {{main|2024–25 FA Cup}} ===Crystal Palace===

As a Premier League team, [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] entered the tournament in the third round. They began their FA Cup journey with a narrow 1–0 home win over [[Stockport County F.C.|Stockport County]]; the lone goal scored by [[Eberechi Eze]].{{cite web |title=Crystal Palace 1-0 Stockport County: Eberechi Eze nets the winner against League One club |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5y41njjpqpt |work=BBC Sport|date=12 January 2025 |access-date=21 April 2025}} Palace then defeated League Two side [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]] 2–0, with goals coming from [[Daniel Muñoz (footballer)|Daniel Muñoz]] and [[Justin Devenny]].{{cite web |title=Crystal Palace beat Doncaster Rovers in FA Cup, will face Millwall |url=https://www.espn.in/football/report/_/gameId/730044 |work=ESPN |date=10 February 2025 |access-date=21 April 2025}} In the fifth round against fellow rivals [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] in the south-east London derby, Crystal Palace striker [[Jean-Philippe Mateta]] was stretchered off just nine minutes into the match following a collision with Millwall goalkeeper [[Liam Roberts]], who was shown a straight red card for striking Mateta in the head with his boot—a challenge that left Mateta needing 25 stitches. With Millwall reduced to ten men, Palace quickly took control, earning a 3–1 victory through a [[Japhet Tanganga]] own goal, followed by goals from Daniel Muñoz and [[Eddie Nketiah]].{{cite web |title=Report & Highlights: Palace blast past Millwall to reach FA Cup quarter-finals |url=https://www.cpfc.co.uk/news/match-reports/live-blog-match-report-highlights-crystal-palace-millwall-march-2025/ |publisher=Crystal Palace |date=1 March 2025 |access-date=21 April 2025}}{{cite web |title=Jean-Philippe Mateta: Crystal Palace offer furious update after sickening head injury |url=https://www.fotmob.com/embed/news/01jn95v7tttt/jean-philippe-mateta-crystal-palace-offer-furious-update-after-sickening-head-injury |work=FotMob |date=1 March 2025 |access-date=21 April 2025}}{{cite web |title=Jean-Philippe Mateta injury: Millwall fans' applause shows apparent support for Liam Roberts after red-card challenge |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13321495/jean-philippe-mateta-injury-millwall-fans-applause-shows-apparent-support-for-liam-roberts-after-red-card-challenge |work=Sky Sports |date=1 March 2025 |access-date=21 April 2025}} In the quarter-finals, Crystal Palace were drawn against fellow Premier League club [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]]. Despite being away at [[Craven Cottage]], Palace comfortably dispatched the south-west London side 3–0, with Eberechi Eze, [[Ismaïla Sarr]], and Eddie Nketiah all getting their names on the scoresheet.{{cite web |title=FA Cup Quarter-finals LIVE: Fulham 0-3 Crystal Palace |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx298987dndt |work=BBC Sport|date=29 March 2025 |access-date=21 April 2025}} In the semi-finals against [[Aston Villa]] at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]], Crystal Palace secured a 3–0 victory courtesy of a goal from Eberechi Eze followed by an Ismaïla Sarr brace. This victory sent Palace through to their third FA Cup final, and their first since [[2016 FA Cup final|2016]], when they were defeated 2–1 by [[Manchester United]], with [[Joel Ward (footballer)|Joel Ward]] the only remaining player from that side.{{cite web |title=Sarr’s sizzlers send Crystal Palace soaring into FA Cup final dreamland |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/apr/26/crystal-palace-aston-villa-fa-cup-semi-final-match-report |work=The Guardian |date=26 March 2025 |access-date=26 April 2025}} ===Manchester City===
{| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center;margin:0" |- |+Manchester City's route to the final |- !scope="col" style="width:25px"|Round !scope="col" style="width:180px"|Opposition !scope="col" style="width:70px"|Score |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|3rd |[[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]] ([[City of Manchester Stadium|H]]) |8–0 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|4th |[[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]] ([[Brisbane Road|A]]) |2–1 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|5th |[[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]] ([[City of Manchester Stadium|H]]) |3–1 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|QF |[[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] ([[Dean Court|A]]) |2–1 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|SF |[[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] ([[Wembley Stadium|N]]) |2–0 |- |colspan="3"|'''Key:''' (H) = Home venue; (A) = Away venue; (N) = [[Neutral venue]] |}
As a Premier League team, [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] entered the tournament in the third round. City began their FA Cup campaign with a commanding 8–0 victory at home against League Two side [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]]. The majority of the goals came from [[James McAtee]], who scored a second-half hat-trick, and [[Jérémy Doku]], who scored a brace, with [[Divin Mubama]], [[Jack Grealish]], and [[Nico O'Reilly]] also contributing to the scoring.{{cite web |title=James McAtee nets hat trick as Man City hammer Salford 8-0 |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/723997 |work=ESPN |date=11 January 2025 |access-date=21 April 2025}} This was their biggest win since defeating [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] by the same score in 2019. City survived an early scare against [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]] in the fourth round, with goals from [[Abdukodir Khusanov]] and [[Kevin de Bruyne]] required to nullify a [[Stefan Ortega]] own goal.{{cite web |title=City fight back to see off Leyton Orient in FA Cup thriller |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/leyton-orient-v-manchester-city-fa-cup-4-match-report-8-feb-2025-63874612 |publisher=Manchester City |date=8 February 2025 |access-date=21 April 2025}} In the fifth round, City defeated [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]] 3–1 despite an opener from Plymouth's [[Maksym Talovierov]] due to two goals by Nico O'Reilly, and a goal and an assist from Kevin de Bruyne.{{cite web |title=Teen O'Reilly helps Man City survive Plymouth FA Cup scare |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/732573 |work=ESPN |date=1 March 2025 |access-date=21 April 2025}} In the quarter-finals, Manchester City were drawn against fellow Premier League team [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]], facing them away from home at [[Dean Court]]. [[Evanilson (footballer, born 1999)|Evanilson]] gave Bournemouth a first-half lead, but for the third match in a row, City mounted a comeback, with second-half goals from strikers [[Erling Haaland]] and [[Omar Marmoush]] securing the victory.{{cite web |title=Marmoush fires Man City into FA Cup semis with 2-1 win over Bournemouth |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/marmoush-fires-man-city-into-fa-cup-semis-with-2-1-win-over-bournemouth-2025-03-30/ |work=Reuters |date=30 March 2025 |access-date=21 April 2025}} In the semi-finals at Wembley, City defeated [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] 2–0 by virtue of goals from [[Rico Lewis]] and [[Joško Gvardiol]]. This marked the first time Manchester City featured in three consecutive FA Cup finals, having previously played in the [[2023 FA Cup final|2023]] and [[2024 FA Cup final|2024]] finals respectively.{{cite web |title=Man City beat Forest 2-0 to reach third straight FA Cup final |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/man-city-beat-forest-2-0-reach-third-straight-fa-cup-final-2025-04-27/ |work=Reuters |date=27 April 2025 |access-date=5 May 2025}} ==Pre-match== The pre-match show featured DJ Tony Perry, supported by the [[Royal Marines Band Service|Massed Bands of His Majesty's Royal Marines]].{{cite web |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2025/may/16/emirates-fa-cup-final-2025-running-order-schedule-20251605 |title=The running order of events at the 2025 Emirates FA Cup Final has been confirmed |website=TheFA.com|publisher=The Football Association|date=16 May 2025 |access-date=17 May 2025}} "[[Abide with Me]]", the traditional pre-match cup final hymn, was sung by Sinead Ashiokai, while Siena MBC performed the national anthem "[[God Save the King]]". ==Match== ===Summary=== [[Pep Guardiola]] named a strong attacking lineup for City, and early on, they dominated proceedings. [[Erling Haaland]] had the first clear-cut chance in the 6th minute when he met a deep cross at the far post, but Palace keeper [[Dean Henderson]] blocked it out for a corner. City continued to dominate and had several corners as both Gvardiol and Akanji had headers saved by Henderson. However against the run of play Crystal Palace hit City on the counterattack, after a clearance upfield by defender [[Chris Richards (soccer)|Chris Richards]] met [[Jean-Philippe Mateta]] who, in a neat one two with [[Daichi Kamada]] then released [[Daniel Muñoz (footballer)|Daniel Muñoz]] to race up the wing and cross in from the right for [[Eberechi Eze]] to first-time volley and score in the 16th minute.{{cite news |title=Football: Kamada helps Palace claim 1st major trophy with FA Cup win |url=https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2025/05/5d18a79d3d7f-football-kamada-helps-palace-claim-1st-major-trophy-with-fa-cup-win.html |access-date=18 May 2025 |work=[[Kyodo News]] |date=18 May 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250518111635/https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2025/05/5d18a79d3d7f-football-kamada-helps-palace-claim-1st-major-trophy-with-fa-cup-win.html |archive-date=18 May 2025|url-status=live}}{{cite news |last1=Herman |first1=Martyn |title=Crystal Palace's Eze seals historic FA Cup final win against Man City |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/crystal-palaces-eze-seals-historic-fa-cup-final-win-against-man-city-2025-05-17/ |access-date=18 May 2025 |work=Reuters |date=18 May 2025 |archive-date=18 May 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250518114604/https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/crystal-palaces-eze-seals-historic-fa-cup-final-win-against-man-city-2025-05-17/ |last2=Cawthorne |first2=Andrew}} Munoz nearly provided a second goal for Palace just three minutes later in another run up the wing in a near identical move, only for [[Ismaïla Sarr]]'s shot to be blocked by the legs of City keeper Ortega. In the 23rd minute, a moment of controversy came in the game when City's [[Erling Haaland]] and Palace goalkeeper [[Dean Henderson]] challenged for a long ball by City's [[Joško Gvardiol]], with Henderson palming the ball away when it was outside the penalty box. Despite Henderson's legs being inside the penalty box; the [[video assistant referee]] reviewed the incident and declined to recommend a red card for Henderson.{{cite news |last1=Johnson |first1=Dale |title=The VAR Review: Why Henderson should have been sent off for DOGSO |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/45193526/the-var-review-dean-henderson-erling-haaland-red-card-dogso |access-date=18 May 2025 |work=ESPN |date=17 May 2025}} However, in the 36th minute City were awarded a penalty after Palace's [[Tyrick Mitchell]] was judged to have fouled City's [[Bernardo Silva]], who had already started to fall when Mitchell performed a sliding challenge; however Henderson blocked the resultant penalty by [[Omar Marmoush]] down to his right, who also saved Haaland's follow-up shot.{{cite news |last1=Hytner |first1=David |title=Crystal Palace stun Manchester City to win FA Cup amid drama and Henderson controversy |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/may/17/crystal-palace-manchester-city-fa-cup-final-match-report |access-date=18 May 2025 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=17 May 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250517185532/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/may/17/crystal-palace-manchester-city-fa-cup-final-match-report |archive-date=17 May 2025}} Doku had a shot saved by Henderson in the 42nd minute and captain [[Marc Guéhi]] cleared the parried shot before City could head it in, but at half time Palace led 1–0. In the second half, City had a chance from the restart when a deep cross was cleared from the back post by Palace defender Chris Richards, preventing a certain Haaland headed goal. Palace then started to threaten the Manchester City goal and had several good chances to double their advantage. A deep throw by Richards in the box in the 49th minute saw Eze's goal-bound shot hit his captain, Marc Guehi, in a packed box, with the resulting injury to Guehi's eye later forcing his substitution ten minutes later. City's [[Bernardo Silva]] had a good chance blocked by Palace in the 55th minute, but just three minutes later, Palace thought they had scored. [[Chris Richards (soccer)|Chris Richards]]' deep throw-in led to confusion in the box, and the resulting ricochet saw Muñoz react quickest to score before Ortega could react to go 2–0 up. However, on checking with VAR, it was later ruled out due to an offside call on [[Ismaïla Sarr]]. [[Daichi Kamada]] then had a chance in the 67th minute after a Palace corner was poorly cleared by City and fell to Kamada outside the box, whose shot whipped just over the bar. As time ticked on, City tried to push for an equaliser as Palace suffered another injury to one of their players. In the 71st minute [[Kevin De Bruyne]]'s shot outside the box pole axed Palace midfielder [[Adam Wharton]] as he blocked the shot. Wharton persevered in the match but was later replaced by [[Will Hughes]] in the 86th minute, Hughes having been a losing finalist to Manchester City when at [[Watford F.C.]] in the 2019 Final. [[Nico O'Reilly]] then had a golden chance for City to score in the 74th minute when he found himself clear on goal in the box, but he took too long to think about his shot, and Palace were able to smother him with their defenders to clear the ball away. A number of substitutions came with 15 minutes left of normal time. Palace striker Mateta was substituted for [[Eddie Nketiah]], a former FA Cup winner for Arsenal in 2020, while City brought on [[Phil Foden]] and [[Claudio Echeverri]] for Silva and Marmoush as Pep Guardiola looked to change things. Echeverri was a surprise inclusion in the squad, but within five minutes of coming on he had a great chance to score when his shot was saved by Henderson in the 81st minute. Munoz then had a shot whip across goal in the 86th minute for Palace before Pep then brought on [[İlkay Gündoğan]] for Silva as City went for broke. There were ten minutes of injury time in the game, during which De Bruyne had a shot at goal in the 92nd minute as City tried to force an equaliser to take the game into extra time. In the 95th minute, Echeverri had two golden chances to score, the first being saved by Palace keeper Henderson, and his second blocked by Palace defenders to prevent a certain goal. Palace then held out fairly comfortably in the final five minutes before the referee finally blew his whistle to end the game and give Crystal Palace their first ever FA Cup at the third time of asking. As Palace went up to collect the Cup unused substitute [[Joel Ward (footballer)|Joel Ward]], who was the last surviving Palace player from the 2016 FA Cup Final and was leaving at the end of the [[Darren Cann (assistant referee)|Darren Cann]] ([[Norfolk County Football Association|Norfolk]]) |style="width:60%;vertical-align:top"| '''Match rules''' * 90 minutes * 30 minutes of [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] if necessary * [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|Penalty shoot-out]] if scores still level * Nine named substitutes * Maximum of five substitutions, with a sixth allowed in extra time{{refn|group=note|Each team was given only three opportunities to make substitutions, with a fourth opportunity in extra time, excluding substitutions made at half-time, before the start of extra time and at half-time in extra time.}} |} ==Post match== Crystal Palace's win was the first major trophy in their history and also meant they qualified for the [[2025-26 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League league phase]], marking the first time the team qualified for a [[UEFA]] competition in their history. They also qualified for the [[2025 FA Community Shield]] to face [[2024–25 Premier League]] champions Liverpool. Manchester City's was defeat for a second consecutive FA Cup finals. Having finished third in the Premier League and exited the [[2024–25 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] in the fourth round and the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] in the knockout play-offs, the defeat meant City, despite winning the [[2024 FA Community Shield]], finished the season without a major trophy for the first time since the [[2016–17 Manchester City F.C. season|2016–17 season]]. Despite the FA Cup winners getting a spot in the Europa League automatically, Palace's participation in Europe was later downgraded to the [[UEFA Conference League]] due to joint-owner [[John Textor]] also owning a stake in French club [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]]. UEFA ruled that Palace were in breach of their [[Multi-club ownership (association football)|multi-club ownership]] rules; because Lyon finished 6th in their league and Palace 12th, Lyon were awarded the Europa League spot.{{Cite web |date=11 July 2025|title=Crystal Palace demoted from Europa League over ownership rules |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/ckg5260zzp2o |access-date=11 August 2025|website=BBC Sport}} This decision was appealed by Crystal Palace but was unsuccessful.{{Cite web |date=22 July 2025|title=Crystal Palace appeal to CAS against Europa League demotion |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/ce8350jl5kgo |access-date=11 August 2025|website=BBC Sport}} On 26 May, Crystal Palace held a victory celebration with an open-top bus victory parade around south London before arriving at [[Selhurst Park]] for a party.{{cite web|url= https://news.croydon.gov.uk/celebration-parade-for-crystal-palace-fc-win-in-croydon/|title=Celebration parade for Crystal Palace FC win in Croydon|date=23 May 2025|work=Croydon.gov.uk|accessdate=19 November 2025}}{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cn4glrevd7ro|title=Crowds cheer on Crystal Palace at victory parade|date=23 May 2025|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=19 November 2025}} ==Broadcasting== The final was televised live in the UK on [[BBC One]], [[ITV1]], [[STV (TV channel)|STV]] and [[UTV (TV channel)|UTV]], and streamed via [[BBC iPlayer]], [[ITVX]] and [[STV Player]]. National radio coverage was provided by [[BBC Radio 5 Live]] and [[Talksport]], with local radio stations [[BBC Radio London]] and [[BBC Radio Manchester]] also broadcasting match commentaries.{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m002c7zm |title=Crystal Palace v Manchester City (17/05/2025) |website=BBC Radio London |access-date=17 May 2025}}{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m002cb0b |title=Crystal Palace v Manchester City |website=BBC Radio Manchester |access-date=17 May 2025}} ==Notes== {{Reflist|group=note}} ==References== {{FA Cup}} {{2024–25 in English men's football}} {{Crystal Palace F.C. matches}} {{Manchester City F.C. matches}} [[Category:2024–25 FA Cup]] [[Category:FA Cup finals]] [[Category:Sports events at Wembley Stadium]] [[Category:2025 in sport in London|FA Cup final]] [[Category:May 2025 sports events in the United Kingdom|FA Cup final]] [[Category:Crystal Palace F.C. matches|FA Cup final 2025]] [[Category:Manchester City F.C. matches|FA Cup final 2025]]
